status: rule erasure selected and integrated; see rule-erasure-measurement.json
privacy: Five local photographs of one roster were used, not five independent rosters. Only aggregate counts appear here; originals, raw OCR and ground truth remain under ignored data/private.

comparisonBasis.imagePreparation: orientation-normalized, maximum 2600 px, matching the scan editor input
comparisonBasis.caution: A smaller review counter is not evidence of more correct students or correctly associated fields.

currentTesseract.measurement: npm run measure:scan-review -- <prepared private image> <ignored output> --reference-date=2026-09-22

approaches.assessment: Reject this prototype as a production default. A crop with 20 candidates and only two flags still missed one true student and added one false row. Row coverage and false-association safeguards need further work.

Best current candidate, but the clearest sample still misses the owner's fewer-than-five target and has two surname errors. A shadowed sample still yields 29 candidates for 20 students. Production integration needs full truth and regression checks.

approaches.offlineBrowserTrial: local inference passed with external network blocked; installed-PWA first-use offline cache was not verified
approaches.assessment: Reject this adapter as a production replacement. Three zero-flag samples each still contained a missed identity and confident wrong fields. Local browser execution was demonstrated, but installed-PWA first-use offline caching was not.

Selected. The row-number rule fused with every surname, so the surname inherited the junk's confidence; erasing only long vertical rules makes the number its own word. With the compound-split presentation fix, the clearest capture reads all 40 name fields exactly with no flags, misread-name rows fall from 10 to 4 across the five captures and no confident wrong name is left without a review block.
approaches.measuredAtCode: the first erasure commit, before the independent review fixes

afterReviewFixes.why: The table-band gate leaves staff-block fragments on samples 1 and 2 as rows to review instead of joining one into a ready-looking staff row; see rule-erasure-measurement.json.

conservativeProductionCandidate.engine: local Tesseract with DPI 180 and guarded TSV fragment joining
conservativeProductionCandidate.note: The fourth private photo has an extra incomplete review row after weak age text is preserved. No real-photo field is reassigned.

nameCellSecondPass.reasonNotIntegrated: Two private visual audits disagree on whether the promoted surname is exact; the other four remain flagged, and unflagged name errors are unaffected.

nameCellVariants.limit: The focused private audit includes a disputed transcription, and no all-person/all-photo truth audit supports promotion. The variant did not change the two unflagged wrong name fields, so a lower flag count alone would not satisfy S4.

allRowSingleWordReread.assessment: Reading every name cell again with PSM.SINGLE_WORD changed no text, left a confident wrong surname, and increased review flags. It cannot resolve the current S4 blocker.

imageScaleSweep.source: original clear private photograph, orientation-normalized; aggregate-only results
imageScaleSweep.comparison: The selected prepared 2600-pixel image has 20 candidates, five flags, one unflagged wrong given name and one unflagged wrong surname. A 2800-pixel image reaches four flags, but doubles the unflagged wrong surnames; the lower counter is not safer.

nextExperiment: Staff-block rows below the student table still fragment on some captures and appear as removable extra rows; a staff exclusion that does not depend on reading the role code is the remaining lever. The shadowed capture (sample 3) keeps most of the remaining flags.
decision: Integrate local vertical-rule erasure before Tesseract (studentScanRules.ts), keep threshold 70 and every reading visible. The earlier DPI 180 and conservative-geometry work remains; rejected variants from 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-25 are listed in targeted-ocr-probes.json.
